skill.name: Vivid, emotive word choice
skill.why: Strong words make readers see and feel exactly what you mean.
skill.how: Read the details around the gap. Pick the strong word that fits them exactly.

steps.say: Biscuit the dog was starving. Here's how she ate.

show.nudge: Had is plain. You can't picture how she ate.
Ate is plain too. Which one lets you see the gulping?

show.text: The dog wolfed down its dinner.

steps.ask: Tap the line that lets you see it happen.
steps.win: Yes! Wolfed down shows her gulping. That's a vivid word.

steps.say: Your turn. Read the clue first.

show.text: Gus hadn't eaten for two whole days.

steps.ask: Which word fits the gap best?

options.reason: Nibbling is tiny, slow bites. He hasn't eaten for two days!
Sniffing isn't eating. He's starving. What would he do?

steps.win: Yes! Two days without food? He'd gobble it.

steps.say: Careful! The strongest word isn't always right. It must fit.

show.text: one tiny bite at a time.

steps.ask: Which word fits the gap best?

options.reason: Wolfed down is strong, but the clue says one tiny bite at a time.
Gobbling is fast. This puppy is sick and takes tiny bites.

steps.win: Yes! Sick puppies nibble. Check the clues, not just the strength.

steps.say: Vivid words can set a feeling too.

show.nudge: Walked is plain. It doesn't make anything creepy.
Looked is plain too. Which word lets you hear something?

steps.ask: Tap the vivid word that makes the cave sound creepy.
steps.win: Yes! Shuffled lets you hear something moving in the dark.

steps.say: Look at what this puppy does.

options.reason: Happy puppies bark and wag. Whimpering is a soft, sad cry.
Angry dogs growl. Whimpering is soft and sad.

steps.win: Yes! Whimpered is sad. Words that carry a feeling are emotive words.

steps.say: Emotive words make you like or dislike something.

show.nudge: Cosy is small in a nice, warm way. That's praise.
Small is plain. It has no feeling in it.

steps.ask: Tap the one that says the writer dislikes the cabin.
steps.win: Yes! Cramped is small and squashed. Same cabin, worse feeling.

encounters.text: Uproar at the Grand Final. The crowd of nearly twenty thousand had been chanting the Rays' song all afternoon. With only thirty seconds left on the clock, the Reef Rays were trailing the Pine Gully Possums by a single point when Rays captain Jax Moana marked the ball directly in front of goal. It should have been the easiest kick of his career. Instead, the umpire's whistle shrieked, and he awarded a free kick to Pine Gully for a push that nobody else in the ground seemed to have seen. The replay on the big screen showed Jax with both hands firmly at his sides. Within seconds, thousands of Reef Rays fans were on their feet, shaking their fists, stamping on the stands and hurling insults across the fence. The crowd ___ the umpire all the way to the change rooms, and the noise was so loud that the Possums' coach covered his ears. Tully, who was there with the crew, later described it as 'the loudest ninety seconds in the history of football, statistically speaking'. The umpire has since admitted that he may have been looking at a seagull. The Possums took the free kick, scored, and won by seven points. Fans say they will remember it for years.

encounters.frame: Gus wrote up the whale rescue for the Field Guide. Tully wrote what three of his words do, but got one wrong.
encounters.text: At dawn on Thursday, a young humpback whale was found stranded on the sandbar at the mouth of Mirage Creek. It was the first stranding there in twenty years. By the time the crew arrived, more than forty volunteers were already there, in a line from the water's edge to the whale. Some of them had driven through the night to help. They splashed buckets of seawater over its skin, hour after hour, to stop it drying out in the sun. By midday, the volunteers' arms ached, and the sand was too hot to stand on barefoot. The whale barely moved. Every so often, it let out a long, low breath that sent a fine mist into the air. Wren knelt by its eye and talked to it quietly, the way she talks to every frightened animal. At two o'clock, the tide finally began to rise. The water crept up around the whale's belly, then its flippers. The volunteers held their breath. Suddenly, with a mighty flick of its tail, the whale surged forward into the deep channel, sending a wave crashing over everyone's boots. A huge cheer erupted along the beach. Gus says he will never wash those boots again. The whale was last seen heading north, towards the open sea.

encounters.text: Zed had spent six months building the greatest castle anyone had ever made in Cubeland Quest. It had a moat, a drawbridge, three secret tunnels and a dragon made of four thousand tiny blocks. Every night after homework, he had added one more tower. On Saturday he invited his cousin Darcy onto the server to see it. Darcy was nine and had only played twice. Darcy looked around for about thirty seconds. Then she pressed one button, and the whole castle disappeared in a cloud of pixels. 'Oops,' she said, not sounding sorry at all. Zed did not shout. He did not throw his controller. He sat completely still, with his jaw clenched so tight it ached and his knuckles white around the controller. When Darcy asked if he wanted to play something else, he didn't answer. When Mum called him for dinner, he walked to the table without a word, sat down and stabbed at his peas. Mum asked if he was feeling all right, and he said 'Fine' in a voice like a closing door. Inside, he ___ for the rest of the evening, though anyone who glanced at him might have thought he was simply quiet. By Sunday morning he had calmed down enough to start building again, this time with a password.
encounters.prompt: Which word fits best in the gap?
encounters.success: Seethed. Seething is boiling with anger inside while staying quiet, like a clenched jaw and stabbed peas.

options.reason: Rejoicing is being full of joy. Zed's castle has just been wiped out, and his jaw is clenched.
Panic is frantic and rushed. Zed sits completely still, then walks quietly to dinner.
Dozing is light sleep. Zed is wide awake, gripping the controller and stabbing his peas.

encounters.frame: Mo made it to the final of Island Junior MasterChef. The Zingfiddle is watching the head judge.
encounters.text: The final round of Island Junior MasterChef came down to Mo and a girl called Priya, and the crew had squeezed into the front row. Mo had made his famous sardine trifle, which nobody had asked for. Priya had made a simple bowl of pumpkin soup. The judges had already sent home a jelly that exploded and a pie with a sock in it. The head judge, a famous chef with a moustache like a broom, tasted Mo's trifle first. He chewed twice, went pale and reached for a glass of water. Then he turned to Priya's soup, and the other two judges leaned forward in their seats. He lifted the spoon slowly and breathed in the steam. He took the tiniest sip and closed his eyes. For a long moment, he didn't move at all, holding the soup on his tongue as if he wanted it to last forever. A slow smile spread under the moustache. He ___ every last spoonful in the same way, taking almost ten minutes to finish one small bowl, while the audience waited in silence. Finally, he set down his spoon and wiped his moustache with a napkin. Mo leaned over to Tully and whispered that he thought it was going well. Tully patted his arm.
encounters.prompt: Which word fits best in the gap?
encounters.success: Savoured. Savouring is eating slowly to enjoy every bit, like tiny sips and ten minutes for one bowl.

options.reason: Devouring is eating fast and greedily. The judge takes ten minutes over one small bowl.
Gulping is swallowing quickly in big mouthfuls. The judge takes the tiniest sips.
Spurning is rejecting something with scorn. The judge smiles and finishes every last spoonful.
